sentence: This project studies how different developmental trajectories lead to a similar endpoint phenotype in human developmental disorders.
This project provides imaging tools that show how immune cells behave and are arranged inside intact tissues such as gut, skin and lung.
This project studies how the Integrator complex regulates mRNA end processing in neuroendocrine prostate cancer and tests nanoparticle-based CRISPR RNA engineering.
This project modifies a firefly enzyme and its small molecule so bioluminescence can image otherwise invisible physiological responses in live animals.
This project tests whether a tracer used for molecular imaging can noninvasively tell apart types of cardiac amyloidosis.
This project studies how transposons, which are mobile genetic elements, cause abnormal splicing across human tissues and diseases.
This project engineers Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cells to secrete a tumor-targeting peptide that helps them infiltrate solid cancers.
This project studies how high levels of Mitotic arrest deficient 1 in cancer affect tumor formation and metastasis.
This project studies the evolution of germinal centers, which are immune structures, to find the genes and pathways needed to form them.
This project tests ways to target T follicular helper cells so that mRNA vaccines against HIV work better in nonhuman primates.
This project studies the molecular architecture of voltage-gated ion channels and how these complex molecules are assembled.
This project uses machine learning to find emergency department patients with opioid misuse so that treatments can reach them.
This project uses imaging, artificial intelligence and computational modeling to study atrial remodeling and why atrial fibrillation returns in patients.
This project uses genomic approaches to understand lung adenocarcinoma, including how genome alterations in individual genes cause the disease.
This project builds a small chip with human cells to study how pulmonary arterial hypertension enlarges the right ventricle of the heart.
This project builds an AI-based method for designing drugs that delay the aging of mesenchymal stromal cells.
This project uses artificial intelligence and the laws of fluid dynamics to measure how fluids flow through the brain to clear waste.
This project uses a patient-derived colorectal cancer chip to study how the microbiome affects tumor response to immunotherapy.
This project brings together investigators who do cancer-related viral research.
This project uses MRI and heavy hydrogen attached to glucose or fatty acids to see how the heart uses energy in patients with ischemia.
